sources.entry: Homer - Dead simple static homepage to expose your server services, with an easy yaml configuration and connectivity check. (Demo) Apache-2.0 Docker/K8S/Nodejs
Homer | A dead simple static homepage for your server

summary.one_liner: Homer is a static, YAML-configured homepage that lists and links your self-hosted services in a searchable dashboard.
summary.what_it_does: Homer generates a static HTML/JS dashboard from a single YAML configuration file (assets/config.yml) that defines your services as links and cards. It supports multiple pages and item grouping, theme customization, and fuzzy search across entries. Keyboard shortcuts let you start searching with "/" and open the first match with Enter, optionally in a new tab with Alt/Option+Enter. It can be installed as a PWA and includes "smart cards" for service status. The dashboard is served by any HTTP server and is run either from a Docker image, a prebuilt release tarball, or a manual pnpm build.
use_cases: Build a homepage linking to self-hosted services
Organize service links into multiple pages and groups
Run a lightweight start page on a home server
Search and launch bookmarked services quickly from the keyboard
Deploy a static dashboard in Docker or Kubernetes
how_to_run: Or use docker-compose with image b4bz/homer, mounting /path/to/config/dir to /www/assets on port 8080
Or download homer.zip from the release page, unzip it, and run: cp assets/config.yml.dist assets/config.yml
Serve the extracted folder with a web server, e.g. pnpx http-server or python -m http.server 8010
Build manually: pnpm install && pnpm build, then serve the /dist directory
notable: Entire dashboard is static HTML/JS driven by one YAML config file
Bind-mounted config directory makes the dashboard easy to edit in place
Fuzzy search and keyboard shortcuts for quick navigation
Environment variables for subfolder hosting, port, and IPv6 toggle
caveats: Must be served over HTTP; opening index.html directly via file:// does not work
Container runs as uid/gid 1000 by default, so the assets directory permissions may need adjusting
